newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close up sharply on firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close up sharply on firmer cash.

text.p: Reports of further strength in cash lumber kept nearby CME lumber futures sharply higher at the close after posting limit gains in July and September, traders said.
Lumber closed $9.40 per tbf higher to $3.00 lower with July up $9.30 at $381.30 and September up most at $364.20. July traded down to $364.90, off $7.10 earlier, before rallying the limit.
Realignment of the spread and a slow housing market weighed on July early but prices turned around on further strength in cash product, traders said.
Random Length quoted cash spruce at $362, up $8 from last Friday and $12 above the last midweek quote. Cash sources said later sales were in the $365 to $370 area.
Some strength also reflected continued concern over labor negotiations and forest fires in Canada, they added.
